title: 1 year of solo dev, 8 hours/day with AI: I built a 5-level Tower Defense demo and need your feedback!
author: SoloDev_Sg
selftext:
**Game:** Magic Animal TD  
**Playtest Access:**[Magic Animal TD on Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4639150/_/)*(Scroll down a bit and click the green "Request Access" button to play instantly!)*

**What is it?**  
Basically, think of it as a cozy Kingdom Rush—but instead of soldiers, you use magical animal defenders. The main twist is a customizable Gem System. 

You can freely equip your heroes and animals with different magical gems to enhance their strengths or cover their weaknesses.

(Note: As for the gem mechanics, only the Hero Gem feature is available in this playtest while I finish developing the Animal Gem system!)

**How do I collaborate with AI?**

My personal philosophy on using AI: "Game design and creative expression must be entirely human-driven, rather than relying on inexplicable, RNG ideas rolled out of an LLM. Based on this human-driven foundation, AI should only be used as a tool to improve production efficiency."

Here is how that translates into my actual workflow:

* **Game Assets:** Since I don't have an art background, I purchase all my unit models, environment assets, and VFX directly from the Unreal Engine Marketplace to ensure everything is highly usable and production-ready.
* **UI Art:** I use AI to assist in generating and refining the 2D UI elements.
* **Coding (The Core Collaboration):** Before starting the actual production, I spent 6 months purely learning coding basics and practicing with the engine. I knew the combat system I envisioned would be complex, so I had to approach the codebase with extreme caution. Because of this foundation, while 100% of the implementation code is written by AI, it acts strictly as my executor. I deeply verify the system architecture and logic flow line by line. From my experience so far, this deep level of control has helped me avoid countless cascading bugs. AI does the heavy lifting of writing the syntax, but I remain the architect.

**Looking for Playtesters!**

After a year of grinding, I finally have a polished 5-level demo ready. I am incredibly excited (and nervous!) to see how real players interact with the mechanics I built.

To cater to different playstyles, the demo includes 4 difficulty settings—so whether you prefer a relaxed, cozy run or a hardcore strategic challenge, you're more than welcome to dive in and test your skills!
